title: Van de Graaff Generator Tour
description: Guided walkthrough of the belt-charge column, isolated sphere, and spark gap.

steps.title: Welcome to the Van de Graaff bench
steps.body: A classroom electrostatic generator: an insulating belt carries charge up a column to an isolated metal sphere. This is a lumped, textbook model — not a high-voltage engineering design.

steps.title: The charging belt
steps.body: A grounded lower comb sprays charge onto the moving belt; an upper comb strips it off near the sphere. Belt current scales with belt speed — try the drive slider and watch belt m/s rise.

steps.title: The isolated sphere
steps.body: Charge accumulates on the sphere's outer surface. Capacitance C = 4πε₀r sets how much voltage builds per coulomb — watch sphere voltage climb as charge (nC) accumulates.

steps.title: Leakage keeps it honest
steps.body: Real air and support insulation aren't perfect — a leakage resistance bleeds charge continuously. Voltage settles where belt current in balances leakage current out, well below breakdown, until a spark resets the balance.

steps.title: Spark gap discharge
steps.body: When the field at the sphere surface exceeds the classroom air-breakdown estimate, a spark discharges part of the stored charge and the cycle restarts. Watch the spark-rate telemetry (Hz) as you raise the drive.
